subject.title: [Bug]: Memory Multimodal Indexing - Gemini API rejects OGG/Opus audio files

question: Should Gemini multimodal memory drop/narrow OGG and Opus support with diagnostics, or should OpenClaw own automatic transcoding to a Gemini-supported audio format before embedding?
rationale: Both fixes are technically plausible but choose different public docs, dependency, provider-cost, and maintenance contracts, so automation should not pick the memory audio policy.

options.title: Narrow Gemini Audio Support
options.body: Document and enforce Gemini-supported audio formats for embeddings, with non-fatal skip or diagnostic behavior for OGG/Opus files.

options.title: Own Audio Transcoding
options.body: Add an ffmpeg-backed conversion path that turns unsupported audio into WAV or MP3 before embedding, including dependency detection and failure handling.

options.title: Defer To Broader Multimodal Design
options.body: Keep this issue open under broader multimodal memory direction until provider-specific media handling is settled across formats.

recommendation.title: Narrow Gemini Audio Support
recommendation.body: Document and enforce Gemini-supported audio formats for embeddings, with non-fatal skip or diagnostic behavior for OGG/Opus files.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice lands closest to the shipped multimodal memory extraPaths feature and public config/docs boundary introduced by the merged multimodal memory work.
